# ScanMyLib HTTP API (phone app + web UI ⇄ api)

Base URL: `PUBLIC_URL` (e.g. `http://192.168.1.10:8765`). JSON everywhere unless
stated. Times are ISO-8601 with offset. IDs are UUIDs (lowercase, hyphenated),
**generated by the client** for documents and pages so that the phone can work
offline and retry safely (all creates are idempotent).

## Authentication

- Phone app: header `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- Web UI: `POST /api/session` with the token → HttpOnly cookie `scanmylib_session`
  (SameSite=Strict, Path=/, 1 year). Either credential is accepted by every
  protected endpoint. State-changing requests authenticated by cookie must also
  carry header `X-ScanMyLib: 1` (CSRF guard; the phone app sends it too).
- The token is random (32 bytes, URL-safe base64), generated on first start and
  stored in `/state/token` (overridable with env `SCANMYLIB_TOKEN`).
- Errors: `401 {"detail": "unauthorized"}`.

Pairing URI (QR code shown by the web UI): `scanmylib://pair?url=<urlencoded PUBLIC_URL>&token=<token>`.

## Public endpoints (no auth)

| Method | Path | Response |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/health` | `{"name": "ScanMyLib", "version": "0.2.3", "api": 1, "apk": {…} or null}`: `version` is the project version (`VERSION`), `api` the level of this contract, `apk` the published APK (below) |
| GET | `/download/scanmylib.apk` | the Android APK (`application/vnd.android.package-archive`), 404 if not built |
| GET | `/`, `/static/…` | web UI |

`apk` describes the APK `/download/scanmylib.apk` serves: `{"application_id": "fr.scanmylib", "version": "0.2.3",
"version_code": 203, "sha256": "…", "size": 12345678, "path": "/download/scanmylib.apk"}`. The api reads it from the
metadata `scripts/build-apk.sh` publishes next to the APK (`scanmylib.json`, with the keys `application_id`,
`version_name`, `version_code`, `sha256` and `size`) and checks each field: `apk` is null without an APK, or without
metadata that holds up, or with the metadata of another APK (not the size of the one published). The app offers the
update when `version_code` is higher than its own and `application_id` is its own; it then checks the downloaded file
against `sha256` and its signing certificate against its own.

## Session

| Method | Path | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/session` | `{"token": "…"}` | `204` + Set-Cookie, `401` if wrong |
| DELETE | `/api/session` | – | `204`, clears cookie |

## Status & pairing

`GET /api/status` →

```json
{
  "version": "0.2.3",
  "ocr": { "reachable": true, "state": "idle", "backend": "vllm", "last_error": null, "gpu": {…} },
  "queue": { "queued": 3, "processing": 1, "error": 0, "done": 120 },
  "library_dir": "/home/user/Documents/ScanMyLib"
}
```

`ocr.state` is the sandbox engine state, or `"unreachable"` when the socket does not answer.

`GET /api/pairing` →
`{"url": "http://192.168.1.10:8765", "token": "…", "pair_uri": "scanmylib://pair?…", "apk_available": true, "apk_url": "http://192.168.1.10:8765/download/scanmylib.apk"}`

`GET /api/pairing/qr.svg` → QR code (image/svg+xml) of `pair_uri`.
`GET /api/pairing/apk-qr.svg` → QR code of `apk_url`.

## Documents

Document object:

```json
{
  "id": "6f1c…",
  "slug": "example-book",
  "title": "Example Book",
  "author": "Jane Doe",
  "kind": "book",                 // "book" | "document"
  "notes": "",
  "unwarp": true,                 // flatten curved pages (UVDoc) when OCRing; defaults to true for books, false otherwise
  "created_at": "…", "updated_at": "…",
  "stats": { "pages": 42, "done": 40, "queued": 1, "processing": 1, "error": 0, "excluded": 0, "duplicates": 0 },
  "coverage": { "ranges": [[1, 12], [45, 60]], "label": "1–12, 45–60", "gaps": [[13, 44]], "min": 1, "max": 60, "unnumbered": 3 },
  "cover_thumb_url": "/api/pages/<id>/thumb",     // first page in reading order, or null
  "folder": "/home/user/Documents/ScanMyLib/example-book"   // host path, display only
}
```

| Method | Path | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/documents` | – | `{"documents": [Document…]}` sorted by `updated_at` desc |
| PUT | `/api/documents/{id}` | `{"title", "author"?, "kind"?, "notes"?, "unwarp"?}` | upsert: `201` created / `200` updated → Document. `title` required on create. Slug is derived from the title at creation and never changes. |
| GET | `/api/documents/{id}` | – | Document + `"pages": [Page…]` in reading order (see below) |
| PATCH | `/api/documents/{id}` | any of `title, author, kind, notes, unwarp` | Document |
| DELETE | `/api/documents/{id}` | – | `204`; folder moved to `LIBRARY/.trash/<slug>-<timestamp>` |
| PUT | `/api/documents/{id}/order` | `{"page_ids": [ids of the reading order, in the wanted order]}` | `200` Document + `"pages"` (same shape as `GET /api/documents/{id}`); `409 {"detail": "page set changed"}`, `422`, `404`. See "Page order" |
| DELETE | `/api/documents/{id}/order` | – | `200` Document + `"pages"`: every `position` cleared, automatic order |
| GET | `/api/documents/{id}/markdown` | – | `document.md` (`text/markdown; charset=utf-8`) |
| GET | `/api/documents/{id}/html` | – | `{"html": "<sanitized HTML of the whole document>"}` |
| GET | `/api/documents/{id}/export.zip?scans=0` | – | zip of the document folder (`scans=1` includes original photos) |
| GET | `/api/documents/{id}/files/{path}` | – | a file inside the document folder (`images/…`, `pages/…`); path traversal rejected |

`pages` order in `GET /api/documents/{id}`: the reading order used for
`document.md` (placed pages, then unplaced ones: see "Page order"), followed
by pages not in the document (`queued`/`processing`/`error`, then `excluded`,
then duplicates), each group by capture time.

`GET /api/documents/{id}/html` holds the pages of `document.md`, in the same
order: an `<h1>` title, then one `<section class="page" data-key="…">` per page,
starting with `<p class="page-marker" data-label="…">`, where `data-key` is the
page's `key` and `data-label` its `page_label` (empty for an unnumbered page);
`<p class="missing-pages" data-range="…">` marks a gap in the numbering
(`data-range`: "13–44", or "13" for one page) and `<h2 class="unnumbered">`
precedes the unplaced pages. These elements hold English text ("Page 42",
"Unnumbered page", "Missing pages: 13–44", "Missing page: 13", "Unnumbered
pages"); their classes and data attributes let the web UI show them in the
user's language. Formulas are `<div class="math-display">` /
`<span class="math-inline">` elements holding the TeX as text. The web UI's
reading view (`#/documents/<id>/read`) is built on this: it links each page
marker to the page (found by `key` in `GET /api/documents/{id}`), lists the
pages and gaps in its page menu, and typesets the formulas with KaTeX.

## Pages

Page object:

```json
{
  "id": "1a2b3c4d-…",
  "document_id": "6f1c…",
  "key": "20261012-201530_1a2b3c4d",
  "session_id": "…", "seq": 3,
  "captured_at": "…", "uploaded_at": "…",
  "status": "done",               // queued | processing | done | error
  "error": null,
  "number": 42,                   // effective page number, null if unknown
  "number_end": null,             // for spreads (two pages in one photo)
  "page_label": "42",             // display label ("xii" for roman front matter, "42–43" for spreads, null)
  "number_source": "detected",    // manual | detected | hint | inferred | null
  "detected_numbers": ["42"],
  "hint_number": null,
  "manual_number": null,
  "excluded": false,
  "duplicate_of": null,           // id of the page that supersedes this one
  "in_document": true,            // part of document.md
  "position": null,               // place chosen by the user on the number line (see "Page order"), or null
  "placement": "number",          // number | manual | session | unplaced; null when not in_document
  "rotation": 0,                  // 0 | 90 | 180 | 270, applied before OCR
  "width": 2480, "height": 3508,
  "ocr": { "engine": "paddleocr-vl-1.6", "duration_s": 2.3, "at": "…", "images": 2, "chars": 2345 },  // null until done
  "thumb_url": "/api/pages/1a2b…/thumb",
  "image_url": "/api/pages/1a2b…/image"
}
```

| Method | Path | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/documents/{id}/pages` | multipart: `file` (required, JPEG/PNG/WebP ≤ 40 MiB), `page_id` (required UUID), `session_id`?, `seq`?, `captured_at`?, `page_number_hint`? | `201` Page (created) / `200` Page (same `page_id` already uploaded — nothing re-done). `404` unknown document, `413`, `415`, `422` |
| GET | `/api/pages/{id}` | – | Page + `"markdown"` (page markdown as stored on disk) |
| GET | `/api/pages/{id}/html` | – | `{"html": "<sanitized HTML>"}` (image URLs point to `/api/documents/{doc}/files/images/…`) |
| PATCH | `/api/pages/{id}` | any of `manual_number` (int or null), `excluded` (bool), `rotation` (0/90/180/270) | Page. Changing `rotation` re-queues OCR. Reassembles the document. |
| POST | `/api/pages/{id}/reprocess` | – | `202` Page (status back to `queued`) |
| DELETE | `/api/pages/{id}` | – | `204`; scan + outputs moved to `.trash`, document reassembled |
| GET | `/api/pages/{id}/image` | – | original scan |
| GET | `/api/pages/{id}/thumb` | – | JPEG thumbnail (max 480 px) |

## Page order

The pages of the reading order (`in_document`: `done`, not excluded, not a
duplicate) are placed on a **number line**, where page n sits at n:

| `placement` | the page's place | |
|---|---|---|
| `manual` | its `position` | set by `PUT …/order` only, cleared by `DELETE …/order` |
| `number` | its effective number: n for page n and for the spread n–n+1; v − 10000 for roman front matter v (before page 1) | |
| `session` | next to its scanning session: d × 0.0001 after the nearest previous page of the session (by `seq`, distance d) that has a position or a number, else d × 0.0001 before the nearest following one | page with neither position nor number; excluded pages are not anchors, duplicates and pages waiting for OCR are |
| `unplaced` | none | e.g. unnumbered pages scanned in a session of their own |

Placed pages are sorted by (place, `captured_at`, `id`); the `unplaced`
pages follow, by (session start, `seq`, `captured_at`), under the heading
"Unnumbered pages" of `document.md` when other pages have a number. When
no page has a place (letters, forms), that is the capture order. So a title
page and a preface scanned just before page 1, in the same session, come
before page 1, and an unnumbered plate scanned after page 12 stays between
pages 12 and 13. A `position` never changes `number`, `page_label`, the
coverage or the duplicates. `placement` is `null` for the pages that are not
`in_document`; their `position`, if any, applies again when they come back
(e.g. after reprocessing).

`PUT /api/documents/{id}/order` — body `{"page_ids": [...]}`: the ids of
**exactly** the pages currently `in_document` (placed and unplaced), each
once, in the order wanted by the user. Otherwise (a page processed, excluded
or deleted since the client loaded the list...) nothing changes and the answer
is `409 {"detail": "page set changed"}`: reload the document and apply the
move again. A malformed body (not a list, not lowercase hyphenated UUIDs,
more than 10 000 ids) gets `422`; an unknown document `404`. Authentication
and the `X-ScanMyLib` header as for every write.

Only the pages that moved get a position: the others keep their automatic
place (`number`, `session` or `unplaced`) and `position: null`, so that the
number line stays intact and pages scanned later still slot in by their
number.

- Numbered pages: the pages of a longest strictly increasing subsequence of
  their natural places (ties: pages without position first) keep their
  place; the other numbered pages get a position.
- Pages with neither number nor position: their automatic places are the
  ones they get when none of them has a position and the other pages have
  the positions computed below. The largest group of them whose places
  already follow the wanted order (between the numbered pages that keep
  theirs; `unplaced` pages only at the end, in their own order; of two pages
  at the same place, not both if pages are moved between them) keeps its
  place if the order is then the wanted one. Otherwise (a page moved away
  from its session drags along the pages placed next to it), as many of them
  as possible keep it: tried by halves in the wanted order, down to single
  pages, while the others are held at their place by a position; a page
  still held at the end loses its position if the order stays the wanted one
  without it. The other pages of this kind moved: they get a position.
- Pages that already have a position keep one, recomputed, except the
  numbered pages kept by the subsequence. `DELETE …/order` clears them all.

Positions are computed from the numbered pages that keep their place: the
k-th of the m pages between two of them, a and b, gets a + (b − a) × k / (m + 1);
the m pages before the first get b − m … b − 1; those after the last
a + 1, a + 2…; 1 … N when no page has a number. When the positions of a run
of pages do not fall between the places of its neighbors that keep theirs
(pages moved between the last front page, at 1 − 0.0001, and page 1), the
run is spread between those places a and b instead: a + (b − a) × k / (m + 1),
or with one neighbor the integers just below b, or just above a. A held page
gets its own place as position.

So moving one numbered page, or one plate, sets one position. Moving an
unnumbered page away from its session also holds, at their place, the pages
of the session scanned just before and just after it, which would otherwise
follow it; moving a numbered page holds an unnumbered page placed after it by
its session; `unplaced` pages that must now come before a page with a place
get one too (unplaced pages always come last). Each order tried is checked
with the ordering itself: the result is always the order sent. The search
stops after about a second of work (very large documents): the pages not
examined keep a position at their place. Sending the current order again
changes nothing; sending the pages in the order of their numbers clears the
positions of the numbered pages. The response is the document with its pages
in the new order; `document.md` follows.

Example: pages 1–5 scanned first, then 2 unnumbered pages (title page,
preface) in a session of their own (`unplaced`, at the end). Moving them
before page 1:

```http
PUT /api/documents/6f1c…/order
Content-Type: application/json

{"page_ids": ["<title>", "<preface>", "<p1>", "<p2>", "<p3>", "<p4>", "<p5>"]}
```

```json
{
  "id": "6f1c…", "…": "…",
  "pages": [
    { "id": "<title>",   "page_label": null, "position": -1.0, "placement": "manual", "in_document": true, "…": "…" },
    { "id": "<preface>", "page_label": null, "position": 0.0,  "placement": "manual", "in_document": true, "…": "…" },
    { "id": "<p1>",      "page_label": "1",  "position": null, "placement": "number", "in_document": true, "…": "…" },
    "…",
    { "id": "<p5>",      "page_label": "5",  "position": null, "placement": "number", "in_document": true, "…": "…" }
  ]
}
```

Page 6, scanned later, is placed at 6, after page 5. Moving page 5 between
pages 1 and 2 instead gives page 5 `position: 1.5` and nothing else.
`DELETE /api/documents/{id}/order` clears every position of the document and
returns the document in the automatic order.

Example 2: 20 unnumbered pages (title page, preface…), pages 1–10 and a plate
after page 5, scanned in one session: the 20 pages are placed by their
session before page 1 (the last one at 1 − 0.0001), the plate after page 5.
3 pages scanned apart later are `unplaced`. Moving these 3 before page 1,
i.e. after the 20 front pages, gives them positions between 1 − 0.0001 and 1
(≈ 0.999925, 0.99995, 0.999975); the 20 front pages and the plate keep
`placement: "session"` and `position: null`. Moved to the very front instead,
they get −22, −21 and −20. Moving then the plate after page 8 gives it 8.5
and nothing else.

## Behavior notes

- Upload is accepted even when the OCR sandbox is down; pages stay `queued`.
- The OCR loop processes pages FIFO by `uploaded_at`; on sandbox `503` it waits
  and retries without counting a failure; on `500` it retries a page at most 3
  times, then sets `status="error"`.
- On startup, pages left `processing` are re-queued.
- When pages get queued, the api calls the sandbox's `POST /v1/load` to pre-warm.
- Errors use FastAPI's default shape: `{"detail": "…"}`.
